newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NatMut says not tempted to buy a bank.
newsitem.headline: NatMut says not tempted to buy a bank.

text.p: Australia's second biggest life office, National Mutual Holdings Ltd, said on Friday it was not interested in buying one of the country's major banks.
Managing director Geoff Tomlinson told Reuters life offices would not be interested in buying banks because of the premium prices banks commanded and because of financial covergence.

"With the degree of convergence taking place in the market place, I don't believe a large life office would be interested in a bank, because I don't think you want to pay the fancy prices for the bank, and vice versa," he said.
Over time, names such as banks and life offices wouldvanish as their businesses continue to overlap, he said.

"We have grown our lending business pretty well off our own initiative over the last couple of years and it's starting to make profits, so we don't think that with the current prices for banks, that it's good value for money," he added.
"We definitely would not be interested in buying a bank and we are not strong advocates at all of bancassurance as such."
Under a recent change to government policy, National Mutual Holdings and its bigger rival, the Australian Mutual Provident Society, would be able to take over one of the major banks.
Australia's four big banks are National Australia Bank (NAB), Westpac Banking Corp, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group and Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
On Thursday, NAB took a swipe at the new government policy on mergers between Australia's financial institutions, saying it had exposed the big banks to foreign takeover.
Under the new policy, the four big banks are prevented from merging, but foreign banks or the two big local life offices can take over one of the big domestic banks.
NAB managing director Don Argus told Reuters on Thursday that merging with a domestic life office could not be ruled out.
